clue.text: Mess about in rescue vessel on lake

blocks.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
Noah's ark rescued the animals from the flood

explanation.surface: Someone fooling around aboard a lifeboat out on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on lake' puts the vessel after the lake's letter, since in a down-style reading of a charade 'A on B' sets A after B.
explanation.definitionFit: To lark about is an informal idiom for behaving playfully or fooling around.

clue.text: Missing man caught, held by all-round rogue

indicators.note: something held by another sits inside its grip, so one piece goes within the other
a rogue letter has gone astray, so these words are to be rearranged into a disorderly new order

blocks.note: taken as written, hyphen dropped
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A vanished villain was caught, held by an all-round scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All-round' looks like praise of the rogue, but it is the anagram fodder. Lord Lucan was a British peer who disappeared in 1974 after his children's nanny was murdered.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Lucan vanished in 1974 and was never found, the most famous missing person in British history.

clue.text: Lover runs rings around yours truly

indicators.note: the rings sit on either side, enclosing the following words

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
two rings, each the ring-shaped letter O
yours truly is a jocular way of saying 'me'

explanation.surface: A lover who keeps running rings round the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo, Shakespeare's young hero, has become a byword for a passionate male lover.

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: that woman is HER, and also means besides

explanation.surface: A report claiming that a certain woman is among the killers too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Killers' suggests murderers; it means weedkillers.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbicides are chemicals that kill plants, so they are killers of weeds.

indicators.note: a thing left without finishing is cut short, losing its final letter

blocks.note: an event is a contest in a sports meeting

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a competition before the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quits' looks like a verb for giving up; it is the adjective in 'we're quits', meaning nothing is owed either way.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits with someone means neither owes the other, which is being square or level.

indicators.note: placing words in another word puts them inside it

blocks.note: to bide is an old verb for endure or wait patiently
to rush is to hurry
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to dismiss haste, in the way that one dismisses the word endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To brush aside an objection is to dismiss or disregard it, an idiom for ignoring.

clue.text: Naughty dog might be so protective

blocks.note: first meaning: risqué, near the knuckle
second meaning: a guarding dog stays right by its chew

explanation.surface: A badly behaved dog that guards its possessions jealously.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful literal reading of the phrase, picturing a dog hovering over what it is gnawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke that is close to the bone is risqué or nearly offensive, an idiom for naughty humour.

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of and
a marriage is an alliance between two people or families

explanation.surface: Asks whether a fling might end in a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the light-hearted reading: a fling followed, in the end, by a formal union.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalliance is a casual romantic or sexual liaison, so a light affair.

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word for sorry is read in the other direction

blocks.note: so means very, as in 'so kind'
sorry in the sense of sad or regretful

explanation.surface: Someone deeply apologetic about their drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodas are fizzy soft drinks, so drinks of a particular kind.

clue.text: It's so long even if it's short

definitions.text: It's so long even if it's short

blocks.clueFragment: It's so long even if it's short
blocks.note: surface reading: a paradox about something tediously long that is actually brief
setter's reading: 'so long' is a goodbye, so this is a parting address, whatever its length

explanation.walkthrough: 'So long' reads as a measure of length; it is the casual phrase for goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A valedictory address given when leaving is essentially a long-form way of saying goodbye.

blocks.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
a mage is a magician or wizard

explanation.surface: An instruction to look for a strange wizard.
explanation.definitionFit: To rummage is to search untidily through a place, turning things over.

indicators.note: with no son means the abbreviation for son is taken away from the word before

blocks.note: unsoiled means not dirty
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone squeaky clean, with the claim that it is no son of theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squeaky clean' reads as one phrase; it splits into the definition and the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge or wheel left without lubricant will squeak, so the word fits by cause and effect.

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so these letters are to be treated as junk and reshuffled

blocks.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Watch your trousers sag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like a noun for trousers or underwear; it is British slang for rubbish, here a call to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen is to become less tight, which is to slacken.

clue.text: How thrilling is extended bike stunt display?

blocks.note: whee! is a cry of excitement
to lie is to stretch out, as a road lies along a valley

explanation.surface: Asks how exciting a long cycling stunt show is.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheelies are tricks in which a rider balances a bike on its back wheel, so a stunt show.

blocks.note: surface reading: a decoration or label on the underside of a house shoe
setter's reading: a slipper is someone who slips, and the item is what was trodden on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slipper' looks like footwear; it means a person who has just slipped, with the cause stuck to their shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit peel is the classic cartoon cause of a fall, found stuck to the shoe of whoever tumbled.

clue.text: Rogue sniper claims one sort of killing

indicators.note: something rogue behaves wildly out of order, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rogue sniper's tally of one victim.
explanation.walkthrough: A crime passionnel is a French term for a crime of passion, usually a killing out of jealousy.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime passionnel is a murder committed in the heat of jealous rage, a particular type of homicide.

blocks.note: taken as written
near means almost, as in a near miss
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: Someone earnestly assuring you they are nearly home.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I'm' as 'I am', so the wordplay says I am beside the home: I, then near, then nest.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in earnest means doing it sincerely and with serious intent.

clue.text: Last pair of horses in posh accommodation for racing event

indicators.note: the last pair means only the closing two letters are kept
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: la-di-da describes an affected, posh manner
the final two letters of horses
the Y is the YMCA, the hostel where travellers stay

explanation.surface: The last two horses housed in luxurious stabling at a race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Y' is a familiar name for a YMCA hostel, so accommodation can stand for Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies' Day is a famous day at Royal Ascot and other meetings when women dress up in hats.

clue.text: Sewer needs essential liquid, then a ladder

indicators.note: a liquid has no fixed shape, so the letters that follow flow into a new form

blocks.note: a need is an essential, something one cannot do without
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drain needs vital fluid, and then a ladder to get down into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' suggests a drain; it is one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: The thread-carrying tool together with its thread is what does the stitching, so it is a thing that sews.

indicators.note: the flogging word goes around the time, enclosing it

blocks.note: to strap is to beat with a leather strap
the digit 1 read as the letter I, followed by PM

explanation.surface: Someone told to sell off a guidebook at about one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' looks like British slang for sell; here it means beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip map is a route map showing a narrow band along a road, used as a travel guide.

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means read upwards, so the word runs from bottom to top

blocks.note: cares are worries or fears

explanation.surface: A mountaineer's fears about an icy peak on the way up.
explanation.definitionFit: A serac is a tall block or ridge of ice on a glacier, a pinnacle of ice.

indicators.note: a thing that parts another splits it in two and sits between the halves

blocks.note: a salt is an old sailor, and AB is an able seaman
re means on, concerning
a circular is a leaflet advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: An instruction to rub salt into round pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular' looks like an adjective meaning round; it is a noun for an advertising leaflet, which splits the word for on.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to wear away or scrape by rubbing.

blocks.note: an Aga is a British brand of range cooker
a fire that is in is still burning

explanation.surface: A stove top that is lit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reads as above; it is the adverb in 'do it over', meaning once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something over means doing it a second time, so the words are synonyms.

blocks.note: single is one, the Roman numeral I
21 down's answer means once more, and bis is the word for twice or encore

explanation.surface: A bird list: one lone bird and a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: Bis, from Latin, is called out to request a repeat performance, so it means again.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a downcurved bill, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Mooring post you measure on river

indicators.note: in a down-style placing, one thing set on another comes after it, so the river's letter is sent first and the rest follows

blocks.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
ye is an old form of you
a peck is a dry measure of two gallons

explanation.surface: Telling a boater they will measure a mooring post on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On river' means after the river's letter, since in this charade the piece placed on another follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rypeck is a pole driven into a riverbed for mooring a punt, an obscure word for a mooring post.

indicators.note: a thing that houses another holds it inside

blocks.note: a bid is an offer at auction
and means with, together
taken as written

explanation.surface: A charity offering shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: Band Aid was the 1984 charity supergroup formed for famine relief in Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: Band Aid is the famous charity record project founded by Bob Geldof and Midge Ure.

clue.text: Crossing ravines, scans for good air quality

indicators.note: the scans stretch across the ravines, holding them in their span

blocks.note: CAT scans are medical body scans
a chine is a deep ravine, a word used on the Isle of Wight and in Dorset

explanation.surface: Scanning ravines to test the quality of the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' looks atmospheric; it means a tune, so the quality is how memorable a melody is.
explanation.definitionFit: Catchiness is the quality of a tune that sticks in the memory, a good property in an air.

indicators.note: the number goes in the city, sitting inside its letters

blocks.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
NY is New York
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone just past fifty living in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and only are synonyms in the sense of merely, as in 'just a minute'.
